principle: Stable editorial intelligence, issue-specific visual invention.

eras.label: Year I / 1933
evidence: Jul contains front/back ink demonstration insert

layout: cover may behave as wrapper rather than single plane
density: range from minimal field to constructivist saturation
irony: technical demonstration can become editorial expression
emergence: attached evidence enters as foreign-local grammar

prompt.cover: Preserve the supplied subject, but treat the cover as an experimental graphic specimen rather than a fixed brand template. Establish a clear modern typographic or photographic proposition, use asymmetrical spatial balance, and permit one production-derived intervention such as a wrapper edge, attached evidence, photolithographic field, specimen fragment or abstract typographic construction. Avoid generic Bauhaus pastiche and copied mastheads.
prompt.emergence: Translate physical attachment and wrapper logic into temporal states: establish the page, reveal an inserted or overlaid evidence layer, allow it to persist as a distinct visual object, then return to the main editorial field without dissolving its identity.

eras.label: Year II / 1934
evidence: Jan cover uses Isard velvet paper
Feb includes 297 x 420 mm Linotype demonstration insert
Jun includes glued quartino with oriental and Asian type specimen
Sep records experimental-edition programme and front/back ink demonstration insert

density: editorial flow alternates between reading field and specimen field
sequence: issue may contain several local visual systems
irony: commercial/technical matter can be re-read as cultural specimen

prompt.cover: Preserve the supplied source image while composing an experimental 1930s Italian graphic-research cover whose identity comes from production intelligence rather than decoration. Use disciplined asymmetry and allow material logic, technical specimen logic or an unexpected format relation to generate the composition. The result may feel tactile or demonstrative, but must not imitate a historical cover, logo or masthead.
prompt.emergence: Treat inserts and specimens as semantic interruptions. Begin with a stable reading field, introduce a differently scaled or differently governed visual object, preserve its local grammar while it is present, then return to the parent field. Do not reduce the event to a generic fade or carousel.

sequence: local graphic identities inside one publication
